title: Who would you share a home with?
note: Domi is a rentsharing app. We help students find the right roommate and split the rent based on how they actually live.

title: We listened to 117 students.
note: We listened to 117 students this week.

title: Sharing rent. Sharing real life.
note: With current rent prices, the best choice is to split the rent. But with who? You have to share your private life, your space, and your daily habits with this person. You need someone you can actually trust.

title: Finding a roommate is exhausting.
note: Right now, finding that person is an exhausting process. You join five Facebook groups, ten WhatsApp chats, scroll through hundreds of ads, and look at blurry photos. It comes down to pure luck.

title: The budget matches. The habits clash.
note: You find someone with the same budget, you sign a lease, and two months later you cannot stand each other. One person studies until three in the morning without headphones. Another leaves dirty dishes in the sink for days. Someone brings guests over every weekend.

title: 3 out of 4 had serious fights.
note: Three out of four students we talked to had serious fights in their first month. None of those fights were about rent. Every single one was about habits: sleep, dishes, noise, and house rules.

title: Why did earlier startups struggle?
note: Before building Domi, we asked a fundamental question. Why did every previous rentsharing startup fail? We analyzed 23 of them, and you can see their full breakdown at the QR code on the screen. In short, they treated students as paying customers.

title: Match. Move to WhatsApp. Leave.
note: They failed because students move to WhatsApp the moment they match. They do not stay on the platform. It is a single-use transaction with near-zero retention. You spend heavy marketing money to acquire a user who leaves after two weeks and never returns, creating a fatal imbalance between customer acquisition cost and lifetime value.

title: Students use Domi for free.
note: Domi works because we treat the student app as our distribution engine, not our direct revenue source. We make the student experience completely free. This is our B2C pro bono journey.

title: Under two minutes. Real boundaries.
note: The onboarding takes under two minutes. I hate shallow gamification, so instead, we made the flow addictive. You answer quick, direct questions about your daily boundaries: sleep hours, kitchen cleaning, guests, smoking, and quiet study time.

title: Your Domi Student Passport.
note: From those answers, we generate your Domi Passport. You see it on screen right now. It displays your verified student status, your home vibe, and your rent guarantors.

title: People you can actually live with.
note: Domi matches students by lifestyle compatibility, lets them chat,

title: Two. Three. Four. Ready to move.
note: and bundles them into ready-to-move-in groups of two, three, or four.

title: Every group shows real demand.
note: By organizing students into vetted cohorts, we build our distribution moat. We capture the actual supply and demand data of the student rental market.

title: B2B tools, on their phone.
note: That brings us to the business owners: the property managers. For them, Domi is an automated intake and portfolio management platform that runs directly on their phone.

title: 300 inquiries. Four hours.
note: When an agency lists a flat in cities like Bucharest, Vienna, Paris, or Amsterdam, they get three hundred inquiries in four hours.

title: Domi handles the first conversation.
note: Our software handles that entire inbound flow through automated calls and messages,

title: The right details, before the viewing.
note: screening move-in dates, verifying documents, and filtering out bad leads.

title: Live demand makes pricing smarter.
note: The real differentiator is that we hold the live market data. Because we see what thousands of students are actively searching and budgeting for, we give property managers dynamic margin optimization. We tell them exactly what price their specific unit can achieve,

title: A tenant profile that fits the home.
note: what tenant profile lowers their vacancy risk,

title: A healthier portfolio, unit by unit.
note: and how to structure their portfolio to maximize net yield.

title: B2B product and sales pipelines.
note: We build with engineering teams and technical partners in Moldova. We have B2B product and sales pipelines, and teams that build software and sell daily. For agencies needing bespoke software, integrations, or enterprise tools, we deliver through those partners.

title: B2C: five years pro bono.
note: I am Lucian. My background is in software engineering, rapid product iteration, and scaling systems. I spent five years teaching pro bono, so I know how the student mind works. In our previous project, we brought in 900 students in two months purely organically, and converted them.

title: Ministry of Justice experience.
note: Through my background at the Ministry of Justice and my diplomatic network, I have the direct relationships to establish institutional partnerships with universities, student associations, and municipal councils.
